  Exam Date & Time: 15-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Network Security [NPT_4148]  
  Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           A student wants to send the message "MEET AT GATE" to a friend using a Caesar  
  Cipher with a shift key of 4.  
  a) Outline the encryption and decryption algorithms, including the role of the key in  
  A)      both processes.                                                                          (5)  
  b) Encrypt the message step by step using the Caesar Cipher technique, showing all  
  intermediate steps clearly.  
  
  B)      A company designs a simple authentication protocol (AP2.0) where the client sends a  
  nonce to the server during login to avoid replay attacks.  
  a) Apply how nonce-based authentication is used to prevent replay attacks during login.  
  b) Examine the sequence of message exchanges between the client and server in the       (5)  
  AP2.0 protocol.  
  c) Use your knowledge of cryptographic randomness to identify one security issue if the  
  nonce is not truly random, and propose an appropriate measure  
  
  2)           A multinational company uses S/MIME to secure internal email exchanges integrated  
  with MIME messages.  
  a) Analyze how S/MIME extends MIME to provide message integrity and  
  A)      authentication.                                                                          (5)  
  b) Compare PGP and S/MIME in terms of key management and trust model.  
  c) Analyze why large enterprises often prefer S/MIME over PGP for business  
  communication.  
  
  B)      An organization wants to securely connect remote employees to its internal network  
  through a VPN tunnel.  
  a) Examine how Tunnel Mode works in IPSec and how it differs from Transport Mode.        (5)  
  b) Demonstrate how private networks and VPNs together ensure secure remote access.  
  c) Show one real-world advantage of using Tunnel Mode in enterprise VPNs.  
  
  3)           An organization uses WPA (with TKIP) for Wi-Fi security but wants to understand how  
  session keys are securely exchanged.  
  a) Outline the four-way handshake process used in 802.11i and how it ensures mutual  
  A)      authentication.                                                                     (5)  
  b) Breakdown the generation of master key in TKIP.  
  c) Analyze how replay attack prevention is achieved in TKIP.

  B)       A telecom provider upgrades from 2G to 3G (UMTS) to improve security and  
  performance.  
  a) Demonstrate the 3G architecture, showing the role of the EPS/UTRAN components.  
  b) Assess the Authentication and Key Agreement (AKA) process in 3G and how it               (5)  
  improves over GSM.  
  c) Report the purpose of message integrity and key hierarchy in 3G security.  
  
  4)            A business suffers a SYN-flood attack that exhausts the capacity of its web server's TCP  
  backlog.  
  a) Analyze the normal TCP three-way handshake and the normal TCP connection  
  A)       termination sequence.  
  b) Analyze how a SYN-flood disrupts this process and outline how SYN cookies (TCP (5)  
  cookie defense) mitigate the attack; include what the server avoids storing when cookies  
  are used.  
  c) Infer why SYN cookies may be suboptimal for some legitimate connections.  
  
  B)       An ISP observes that its customers are suffering from data exfiltration and spoofed IP  
  attacks. To address this, the ISP considers implementing egress filtering and distribution  
  route filtering.  
  a) Demonstrate how egress filtering and distribution route filtering work to prevent  
  network attacks.                                                                           (5)  
  b) Apply your understanding of routing security to describe how route filtering works,  
  and demonstrate how shortcomings in distributed route filtering could impact legitimate  
  network traffic.  
  
  5)            A merchant accepts Bitcoin payments online and wants to ensure all received  
  transactions are valid and irreversible.  
  a) Analyze the process of a Bitcoin transaction, describing inputs, outputs, and unspent  
  A)       transaction outputs (UTXO).  
  b) Infer how confirmation and number of confirmations help protect against double           (5)  
  spending attacks.  
  c) Outline what might happen if a user attempts to spend the same Bitcoin in two  
  different transactions before confirmation?  
  
  B)       A healthcare company is using cloud computing to store patient data and wants to ensure  
  data privacy even while processing sensitive information.  
  a) Analyze the Cloud Computing Reference Architecture, highlighting the roles of cloud  
  consumer, provider, and broker.  
  b) Breakdown the concept of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and how it protects (5)  
  data in cloud environments.  
  c) Outline a simple FHE scheme and mention one potential application in cloud data  
  analytics.
